task.title: Compare long numeric prerelease identifiers without int conversion (python-semver issue #487)
task.statement: python-semver (src/semver, BSD-3) is a semantic-versioning library whose central class is semver.version.Version (also exported as semver.Version). Bug report (upstream issue #487): Version.is_valid("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000) is True, but Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000).compare(...) raises ValueError, because Version._nat_cmp in src/semver/version.py converts every all-digit prerelease identifier with int() and CPython refuses int conversion of strings longer than 4300 digits. Fix the prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so that it never converts a long ASCII numeric identifier to an int, while keeping the existing ordering rules exactly. Required semantics of the prerelease comparison: identifiers are the dot-separated parts of the prerelease string (an empty or None prerelease has one empty identifier); an identifier consisting only of ASCII digits is numeric and compares by its decimal value, computed without int(): strip leading zeros (an all-zero identifier becomes "0"), compare by length first and then lexicographically; a numeric identifier is lower than any non-numeric identifier; two non-numeric identifiers compare as plain strings; when every identifier of the shorter list is equal, the longer list is higher. Preserve the constructor's legacy behaviour: Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=...) accepts identifiers with leading zeros and identifiers written with non-ASCII decimal digits (str.isdigit() is true), and such non-ASCII digit identifiers keep comparing by their int() value, so "١٢" compares equal to "12" and "１２" is lower than "13"; an identifier for which str.isdigit() is true but int() fails (for example "²") must still make compare() raise ValueError, eagerly, even when an earlier identifier would already decide the order, but only when the core versions are equal: a difference in major, minor or patch is decided before the prerelease is examined, so Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True. Keep everything else unchanged: Version.parse keeps rejecting non-canonical prereleases such as "01", "01.2", "١٢" and "１２" with ValueError; build metadata is ignored in comparisons; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same core version without one; the prerelease attribute is stored as given. Do not change parsing, the optional native parser, tests, docs or packaging files, and keep the whole existing pytest suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: With v = "0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000: Version.is_valid(v) is True; Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0; compare(v, "0.0.0-2") == 1 and compare("0.0.0-2", v) == -1 (no ValueError).

Ordering of long numeric prereleases with Version.parse("0.0.0-" + x): "9" * 4999 < "1" + "0" * 4999; "1" + "0" * 4998 + "1" < "1" + "0" * 4998 + "2"; "1" * 5000 < "alpha"; "alpha." + "1" * 5000 < "alpha." + "1" * 5000 + ".1". For each pair low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1 and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
Build metadata is ignored and release order is preserved: with version = Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000), version == version.replace(build="other") and version < Version(0, 0, 0).

Constructor prereleases compare with the legacy rules, as Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)): ("0001", "1") -> 0; ("000", "0") -> 0; ("02", "10") -> -1; ("01.2", "1.2") -> 0; ("2a", "10a") -> 1; ("01a", "1a") -> -1; ("-1", "0") -> 1; ("", None) -> 0; ("١٢", "12") -> 0; ("１２", "13") -> -1; ("1٢", "12") -> 0; ("٠٠١", "1") -> 0; the reverse comparison gives the negated result and both .prerelease attributes are stored as given.
Version.parse("0.0.0-" + p) raises ValueError for p in ("01", "01.2", "١٢", "１２").
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)) raises ValueError for (left, right) in (("²", "2"), ("a.²", "b.0"), ("a.0", "b.²")).
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True (the core comparison decides before the prerelease is examined).
The existing pytest suite in tests/ passes unchanged.

spec.restated_task: Fix prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so ASCII numeric identifiers of arbitrary length compare by normalized decimal strings without integer conversion, preserving numeric precedence, string ordering, identifier-list ordering, and all existing public behavior. Retain permissive constructor inputs, legacy integer-value comparison and eager conversion errors for non-ASCII digit identifiers, core-version comparison before prerelease examination, strict parsing, ignored build metadata, and release precedence. Only comparison-related implementation in src/semver/version.py may change.

interface_contract.name: semver.version.Version / semver.Version
interface_contract.signature: Version(major: SupportsInt, minor: SupportsInt = 0, patch: SupportsInt = 0, prerelease: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None, build: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None)
interface_contract.behavior: Keep constructor behavior unchanged: convert core parts with int(); retain None for absent prerelease/build and otherwise apply str(). String prereleases, including leading zeros, Unicode digits, empty identifiers, and invalid SemVer text, remain accepted and stored unchanged. Comparison must not mutate stored attributes. VersionInfo remains the existing alias.
error_cases: ValueError: a converted core component is negative.
TypeError or ValueError: existing core-component int() conversion fails; preserve existing behavior.
No constructor validation error is introduced for non-canonical prerelease strings, including '²'.

interface_contract.name: Version._nat_cmp
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve this existing internal comparison entry point. Split each operand on dots, treating None and '' as one empty identifier and retaining empty parts. A nonempty identifier containing only ASCII digits is numeric: remove leading ASCII zeros, normalize all zeros to '0', and compare decimal values by normalized length then lexicographic order, without int() conversion. An identifier containing non-ASCII characters for which str.isdigit() is true retains legacy int(identifier) conversion semantics and numeric classification; compare its value correctly against both ASCII and other legacy numeric identifiers. All remaining identifiers compare as Python strings. Numeric identifiers precede non-numeric identifiers. Compare corresponding identifiers until unequal; otherwise compare identifier counts. Return exactly -1, 0, or 1. Validate all legacy numeric conversions in both operands before returning an ordering result, including identifiers beyond a decisive prefix or beyond the shorter operand.
error_cases: ValueError: any non-ASCII identifier satisfying str.isdigit() cannot be converted by int(), including '²'; propagate eagerly regardless of earlier identifier differences.
Preserve runtime int() failures for non-ASCII digit identifiers, including applicable integer-string conversion limits; the unlimited-length guarantee applies to ASCII numeric identifiers.
No ValueError solely because an ASCII numeric identifier exceeds the interpreter's integer-string conversion limit.

interface_contract.name: Version.compare
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve accepted operands and coercion: strings/bytes are parsed, dictionaries and tuples/lists construct versions, and existing compatible Version instances are accepted. Compare (major, minor, patch) first and return immediately when unequal. For equal cores, perform eager prerelease comparison as specified by _nat_cmp before resolving absent-prerelease precedence. None and '' are equivalent absent prereleases; a nonempty prerelease is lower than an absent prerelease. Ignore build metadata. Return exactly -1, 0, or 1.
error_cases: TypeError: unsupported comparison operand type, preserving existing behavior.
Existing parsing or construction exceptions: operand coercion fails.
ValueError: equal-core operands contain a legacy numeric prerelease identifier whose int() conversion fails, even when an earlier identifier or release absence would determine precedence.
No prerelease conversion error when already-constructed operands differ in major, minor, or patch.

interface_contract.name: Version comparison operators
interface_contract.signature: __eq__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __ne__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __lt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __le__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __gt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __ge__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool
interface_contract.behavior: Continue deriving results from compare(), including long numeric identifiers and sorting. Preserve the existing decorator's NotImplemented behavior for unsupported operands and dictionaries/tuples/lists that cannot construct a version.
error_cases: ValueError: propagate prerelease conversion failures from compare() for otherwise accepted operands.
Preserve existing Python operator fallback and error behavior after NotImplemented.

interface_contract.name: semver.compare
interface_contract.behavior: Continue delegating to Version.parse(ver1).compare(ver2), returning exactly -1, 0, or 1 with the corrected long-identifier behavior. Preserve the existing deprecation warning.
error_cases: Preserve parsing and comparison exceptions for invalid inputs.
No integer-conversion-limit ValueError for valid ASCII numeric prereleases.

interface_contract.name: Version.parse
interface_contract.signature: @classmethod parse(cls: Type[T], version: String, optional_minor_and_patch: bool = False) -> T
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged. Accept canonical ASCII prereleases of arbitrary identifier length, preserve their text, retain bytes handling and optional minor/patch behavior, and leave optional native parser dispatch untouched.
error_cases: ValueError: invalid SemVer input, specifically prereleases '01', '01.2', '١٢', and '１２'.
TypeError: unsupported input type.
Preserve all other existing decoding, parsing, and construction errors.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_valid
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged: return True when parse succeeds and False when parse raises ValueError. A valid 5000-digit ASCII numeric prerelease returns True.
error_cases: Preserve propagation of exceptions other than ValueError from parse().

interface_contract.name: Version.replace
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged: return a new version with requested parts replaced. Replacing only build metadata does not change comparison equality, including for long numeric prereleases.
error_cases: TypeError: unknown replacement keys.
Preserve existing constructor errors for replacement values.

acceptance_criteria: 1. With v = '0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000, Version.is_valid(v) is True, Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0, semver.compare(v, '0.0.0-2') == 1, and semver.compare('0.0.0-2', v) == -1, without ValueError.

2. Parse each pair of prereleases using the '0.0.0-' prefix: ('9' * 4999, '1' + '0' * 4999), ('1' + '0' * 4998 + '1', '1' + '0' * 4998 + '2'), ('1' * 5000, 'alpha'), and ('alpha.' + '1' * 5000, 'alpha.' + '1' * 5000 + '.1'). Each pair must satisfy low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1, and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
3. With version = Version.parse('0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000), version == version.replace(build='other') and version < Version(0, 0, 0).

4. For equal-core constructor versions, the following (left, right, expected) cases hold: ('0001', '1', 0), ('000', '0', 0), ('02', '10', -1), ('01.2', '1.2', 0), ('2a', '10a', 1), ('01a', '1a', -1), ('-1', '0', 1), ('', None, 0), ('١٢', '12', 0), ('１２', '13', -1), ('1٢', '12', 0), and ('٠٠١', '1', 0). Reverse comparison returns the negated result, and both stored prerelease attributes equal their original inputs before and after comparison.

5. Constructor prereleases '0' * 5000 and '0' compare equally; '0' * 5000 + '12' and '12' compare equally; '0' * 5000 + '12' and '١٢' compare equally. A 5000-digit nonzero ASCII numeric identifier compares above '١٢'. These comparisons must not convert the ASCII identifier to an integer.

6. Identifier boundaries and empty parts are preserved: Version._nat_cmp('', None) == 0, Version._nat_cmp('a', 'a.') == -1, Version._nat_cmp('a..b', 'a.b') == -1, and Version._nat_cmp('0', '') == -1. Public comparison still places prerelease '0' below an absent prerelease.
7. Version.parse('0.0.0-' + p) raises ValueError for every p in ('01', '01.2', '١٢', '１２'); Version.is_valid returns False for those same version strings.

8. Equal-core constructor comparisons raise ValueError for ('²', '2'), ('a.²', 'b.0'), and ('a.0', 'b.²'), and for their reversals. Also require the error for ('a', 'a.²'), ('²', '²'), and ('²', None), demonstrating eager validation beyond a matching prefix, identical inputs, and release absence.

9. Already-constructed versions with prerelease '²' compare by core without raising when any decisive core component differs: (0, 0, 0) is below (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (0, 0, 1). Forward compare returns -1, reverse returns 1, and the corresponding less-than expressions are True.

10. Run the long-identifier regression checks with an active 4300-digit integer conversion limit on Python runtimes supporting that limit. The implementation must neither alter the interpreter limit nor require disabling it. Source review must confirm ASCII numeric comparison uses zero normalization, length, and lexicographic ordering rather than integer conversion or another numeric-conversion workaround.

11. All existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged; the repository's configured pytest suite continues to pass. Existing operand coercion, comparison errors, aliases, parsing, constructor behavior, and unrelated version operations remain unchanged.
12. The implementation diff is confined to comparison-related changes in src/semver/version.py; no tests, documentation, parsing logic, native-backend integration, or packaging files are modified.

limitations: Profile 'development': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.
